description: We are a team of passionate CSE students and technology enthusiasts interested in space, AI, IoT, software development, and solving real-world problems. We aim to combine creativity, research, and technical skills to build an innovative solution for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. We value teamwork, communication, and learning, and welcome motivated members who are ready to contribute and grow together.
summary: We built AstraVex, an interactive 3D mission exploration and aerospace education platform covering 18 verified NASA and international missions across the Moon, Mars, and Deep Space. It empowers students, educators, and space enthusiasts worldwide by transforming complex, static aerospace archives into visceral, hands-on scientific simulations. Powered by Three.js WebGL rendering, real-time NASA Open Data APIs, and Keplerian orbital physics solvers, AstraVex combines vehicle-accurate launch and landing trajectories with an AI-guided flight director and interactive scientific instrument labs. Live project - https://astravex-0-1-ctg.onrender.com/
details:
1. What does it do or how does it work?

AstraVex SEE is an interactive, browser-based 3D aerospace exploration and educational laboratory covering 18 verified NASA and international missions across The Moon, Mars, and Deep Space.

It operates on a strict 5-stage mission flight pipeline:

  1. Home Command: A real-time 3D planetary system with accurate solar lighting and ephemeris tracking.
  2. Destination & Mission Select: Filtering expeditions by planetary theater and inspecting mission objectives.
  3. Vehicle-Accurate Launch Simulation: Interactive rocket launches matched to each spacecraft’s real booster stack (Saturn V, SLS Block 1, LVM3-M4, Ariane 5, Atlas V, Falcon 9) with animated staging, fairing jettison, and Mach-diamond exhaust physics.
  4. EDL vs. Orbital Insertion: Authentic Entry, Descent, and Landing (EDL) sequences (sky-cranes, retrorockets, lunar modules) for surface landers, and Mars/Lunar Orbit Insertion (MOI/LOI) burns for orbital spacecraft.
  5. Interactive 3D Hardware Inspection: 360° inspection of Draco-compressed 3D models with clickable subsystem markers, 8K Jezero Crater panoramas, and voice debriefs.

Under the hood, AstraVex is powered by J2000 Keplerian astrodynamics solvers (E.M. Standish / NASA JPL) and the Vis-Viva equation to compute instantaneous planetary distances, one-way light delays, and orbital velocities in real time, while streaming live telemetry from official NASA APIs.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Transforms Dense Data into Visceral Physics: Replaces dry tables and static PDF archives with hands-on, vehicle-accurate 3D simulations.
  • Hands-On Science Lab: Features 11 interactive physics simulators, allowing users to ablate Martian rock with SuperCam’s LIBS laser, extract oxygen with MOXIE, record seismic marsquakes with InSight, and measure lunar regolith temperature with Chandrayaan-3’s ChaSTE probe.
  • Direct NASA Open Data Integration: Surfaces live raw photo downlinks, camera Sol manifests, and real-time ISS orbital coordinates directly into the UI.
  • Zero-Barrier Accessibility: 100% web-based with no installations, account creation, or paid licenses required. Runs smoothly on standard laptops, tablets, and school computers via WebGL.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

  • Democratizing Space Education: Making NASA’s rich history and ongoing planetary missions intuitive and exciting for students, teachers, and space enthusiasts worldwide.
  • Inspiring the Artemis Generation: Bridging the gap between passive textbook reading and active engineering exploration by letting students act as virtual flight controllers.
  • Global Scalability: Designed for classroom presentation and interactive self-learning across schools with varying internet bandwidths, supported by full client-side fallbacks.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Languages: TypeScript, JavaScript (Node.js ES Modules), HTML5, CSS3.
  • Frontend Frameworks & 3D: React 18, Three.js, React Three Fiber (@react-three/fiber), @react-three/drei, Tailwind CSS, Framer Motion, Lucide React.
  • Backend & APIs: Express.js, Node.js, Google Generative AI SDK (@google/generative-ai), Dotenv, CORS.
  • 3D Graphics & Compression: Google Draco 3D WASM compression decoder, Blender for GLB/GLTF model optimization and origin centering.
  • NASA & Space APIs: NASA Image and Video Library (images-api.nasa.gov), NASA Mars Rover Photos API, NASA Mars Raw Images RSS Feeds, NASA DONKI Space Weather, Where The ISS At? API, and JPL Solar System Dynamics (SSD) Horizons.
  • AI Engine: Google Gemini Generative AI (Flash & Pro models) for dynamic storytelling, flight director dialogue, and science quizzes.
  • Testing & Deployment: Vite 5 build tool, automated Node.js test runners (122 passing integrity and astrodynamics tests), Git, GitHub, and Render Cloud Hosting.
  • Hardware: Standard development PCs running WebGL 2.0 GPU hardware acceleration.

5. How is your project creative?

  • Vehicle & Staging Authenticity: Unlike existing apps that show generic rocket animations or mix lunar and Martian rovers in the same scene, AstraVex pairs each spacecraft strictly with its real historical launch vehicle, ascent profile, and landing physics.
  • Conversational Flight Director : An interactive AI flight director that remembers the explorer’s name, narrates mission milestones, answers aerospace questions, and debriefs users on telemetry anomalies.
  • Dual-Engine Zero-Hallucination Architecture: Rather than letting generative AI invent facts, AstraVex binds Gemini AI directly to verified NASA databases, paired with deterministic local fallbacks so scientific facts remain 100% accurate even offline.
  • Sensory & Audio Immersion: Features authentic Apollo Quindar radio beeps, rocket thrust acoustics, and responsive audio ducking during voiceover narrations.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  • Scientific Rigor & Verification: Every coordinate (e.g., Jezero Crater at 18.44°N, 77.45°E; Shiv Shakti Point at 69.37°S, 32.35°E) and instrument specification was cross-verified against official NASA and ISRO mission logs.
  • Privacy & Safety (Zero-Auth Architecture): We intentionally avoided collecting passwords, emails, or personal data. Explorer names are kept strictly as temporary session state in the browser.
  • WebGL & GPU Optimization: To ensure smooth 60 FPS performance on modest hardware, we clamped device pixel ratios (dpr={[1, 2]}), eliminated heap allocations inside useFrame render loops, and compressed all 3D assets with Draco WASM.
  • Resilience to Network Drops: Built a multi-tier fallback system—if an external NASA API or AI quota limit is reached, AstraVex instantly transitions to deterministic local science data without interrupting the student's journey.
